in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, could you tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm looking to claim for one child. My son Alex is 19 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Since Alex is 19, I need to ask a few more questions, as Child Benefit eligibility for children aged 16-19 depends on their education or training status.

Is Alex currently in full-time non-advanced education (such as A-levels, NVQs up to level 3, or similar) or on an approved training course? If so, could you tell me a bit more about what he's studying or training for?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he's in sixth form college studying for his A-levels.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you. Sixth form college studying A-levels counts as qualifying full-time non-advanced education.

I have a couple more questions:

When did Alex turn 19? (I need to know this because there are specific rules about when Child Benefit stops for children who turn 19 while in education.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He turned 19 in February this year.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. I have one more important question about Alex's education:

When is Alex expected to finish his A-levels? (For example, will he be completing them this summer, or does he have another year to go?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's finishing them this summer - he'll be done in June.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Let me also check the specific rules about Child Benefit when a child turns 16, as this will clarify the rules for children who turn 19 while in education.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for your patience. I now have all the information I need to assess your eligibility.

Just to confirm a couple of final details:

1. Does Alex live with you?
2. Is Alex receiving any benefits in his own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives with me at home. And yes, he does receive Universal Credit in his own name.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for confirming those details. Based on the information you've provided, I now have enough to make an assessment of your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm afraid you are **not eligible** for Child Benefit for Alex.

**Here's why:**

Normally, you can continue to receive Child Benefit for a child up to age 20 if they remain in approved full-time non-advanced education, such as A-levels. Alex does meet that education requirement.

However, the rules state that you cannot receive Child Benefit for a child aged 16-19 if they receive certain benefits in their own right, including **Universal Credit**. Since Alex receives Universal Credit in his own name, this disqualifies him from Child Benefit eligibility, regardless of his education status.

If Alex's circumstances change in the future (for example, if he stops claiming Universal Credit), you may wish to reassess your eligibility at that time. If you have any questions or need further clarification, you can contact the Child Benefit Office directly.

I'm sorry I couldn't bring you better news. Is there anything else I can help you with?
